input: what does go env do
output: go env prints the settings that configure the go toolchain, such as the target operating system, the module cache location, and where binaries are installed

input: what does go version do
output: go version prints the release of the go toolchain installed on your machine, which matters when code needs a newer language feature

input: what does go clean do
output: go clean removes files the go command created; flags like -cache or -testcache clear just one cache, and plain go clean removes binaries built by go build

input: what does go list show
output: go list prints information about your code; go list ./... shows the local units of code and go list -m all shows every module in the dependency graph

input: what does go mod download fetch
output: go mod download fetches the modules listed in go.mod into the local module cache without building anything, so later builds work offline

input: what does go mod verify check
output: go mod verify checks that every module in the cache matches its recorded checksum and reports any that were changed or corrupted

input: what does go mod graph do
output: go mod graph prints the full dependency graph, one line per module showing what each module requires

input: how does go vet differ from go test
output: go vet analyzes your code for suspicious patterns without running it, while go test compiles and runs your tests and reports pass or fail for each set of tests

input: how does gofmt differ from go vet
output: gofmt only rewrites your source into the standard format, while go vet analyzes what the code means and warns about likely bugs that formatting cannot catch

input: how does go get differ from go install
output: go get adds or upgrades a dependency in your module, while go install builds a program and places the resulting binary in your bin directory

input: what does gofmt's l flag list
output: the l flag makes gofmt list the files whose formatting differs instead of rewriting them, which is how you check formatting in scripts

input: what does gofmt's w flag rewrite
output: the w flag makes gofmt rewrite each file in place with the standard formatting

input: what does go test print with -v
output: the v flag makes go test print each test by name with its result as it runs, instead of staying quiet until a failure

input: what does go test's -run option select
output: the run flag takes a name pattern and runs only the matching tests, which is how you run a single test out of a whole suite

input: what does go test's -cover option measure
output: the cover flag makes go test report what fraction of your statements the tests exercised, printed as a percentage

input: what does go build's o flag name
output: the o flag sets the name and location of the binary that go build writes, instead of using the default name from the directory

input: what does go doc display
output: go doc prints the documentation of a library or a single symbol right in your terminal, the same text that is published online for it

input: what does go mod init do
output: go mod init starts a new module by writing a go.mod file with the module path you give it; run it once in the root of a new project

input: how does go mod tidy differ from go mod download
output: go mod tidy rewrites go.mod so it matches the imports in your code, while go mod download only fetches the already listed modules into the local cache

input: what does the cache flag to go clean do
output: the cache flag tells go clean to delete the build cache, so the next build recompiles every unit of code from scratch

input: what is a build cache in Go
output: the build cache stores the results of compiling code, so a later build can skip everything whose inputs have not changed

input: what does go env print
output: go env prints the toolchain configuration: operating system, architecture, module cache path, and where installed binaries go

input: what does a PASS line mean in go test output
output: PASS means every test in the run succeeded; the ok line before it shows the module path and how long the run took

input: what does a FAIL line mean in go test output
output: FAIL means at least one test failed; the lines above it name the failing test with its file, line number, and failure message

input: what does the error no required module provides package mean
output: it means your code imports a library that is not listed in go.mod; add it with go get or run go mod tidy so the module requirements match your imports

input: what does go vet warn about
output: go vet warns about suspicious code it finds by analysis, like unreachable code, bad format strings, or copying a lock, printing the file and line for each

input: what does a failing go test print
output: a failing test prints the test name, the file and line of the failure, and the message, followed by a FAIL line for the tested code

input: what does go build do with multiple packages
output: given a pattern like ./... go build compiles everything to check for errors but throws away the resulting binaries, since only a main program would produce one
